frontmatter.name: spec-plan-sync-implicit-scope
frontmatter.description: Plan deve validar file coverage contra spec antes de estruturar tasks. SCRUM-73 omitiu chat/message-bubble.tsx que estava em escopo implícito (apps/web/src excluding marketing).

memory_entries_to_create.body:
# Spec-Plan Sync: Implicit File Scope

Plan task structure deve materializar todos arquivos em escopo ANTES de começar a estruturar tasks.

## Problem

SCRUM-73 spec: "Refactor todas as cores em apps/web/src (excludes features/marketing)". Plan não extraiu lista explícita de arquivos afetados. Resultado: chat/message-bubble.tsx (que tinha `text-red-400 → text-destructive`) foi omitido do plan.

Discovery: residual search no final (Step 4 de QA) identificou arquivo faltante.

## How to apply

WRITE_PLAN phase, antes de estruturar tasks:

1. **Spec tem "In scope" / "Out of scope" seções explícitas?**
   - Se sim: use diretamente
   - Se não (regex/pattern only): proceder com step 2

2. **Extract matched files:**
   ```bash
   rg "<pattern>" <dir> --files | sort
   ```
   Example: `rg "bg-emerald|bg-amber|text-blue" apps/web/src --files | grep -v marketing`

3. **Criar plan section "File Structure" (tabela):**
   - File path
   - Action (Modify/Create/Delete)
   - Responsible task
   - Lines estimate

4. **After tasks written: coverage check**
   - Count files in table
   - Count files covered by tasks
   - If covered < total: identify gap + assign to task or mark "deferred"
   - Goal: 100% coverage or explicit deferral

5. **Notate in plan intro:**
   ```
   **File coverage:** 32/32 files extracted and assigned to tasks
   ```

## Success signal

No after-action report deve mencionar "file omitted from plan that was in spec scope". Next large refactor tem "File coverage: X/Y" section.

## Related

- [[bens-implementation-flow]] (update WRITE_PLAN section with checklist)
- SCRUM-73: chat/message-bubble.tsx omission

frontmatter.name: branch-behind-during-pr-development
frontmatter.description: Solo dev em worktree pode ficar behind main se múltiplos PRs mergearem durante implementação. SCRUM-73 ficou behind quando 3 PRs (#318-#320) + chore (#321) mergearam em ~4.5h. Code review vê diff confuso.

memory_entries_to_create.body:
# Branch Behind Main During PR Development

Solo dev em worktree desenvolvendo feature X enquanto PRs Y, Z, W mergeam em main = diff confusa + rebase surprise.

## Problem

SCRUM-73 executou em ~4.5h em worktree. Durante esse tempo, 3 PRs (#318, #319, #320) + 1 chore (#321) mergearam em main. Quando iniciada CODE_REVIEW, branch estava ~4 commits behind main. Code reviewer reportou "businessSegment removido em diff" — na verdade era branch behind, não remoção real.

Rebase resolveu clean, mas causou fricção.

## How to apply

Phase 5-7 (IMPLEMENT → CODE_REVIEW) workflow pra worktree:

1. **Antes de CODE_REVIEW (Phase 7 entry):**
   ```bash
   git fetch origin
   git rebase origin/main
   ```

2. **Se merge conflicts:**
   - Resolve conflicts locally
   - Re-run tests: `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
   - Confirm no behavior regression
   - Commit rebase resolution

3. **If rebase clean (no conflicts):**
   - Diff será meramente "refactor(web): X Y Z"
   - Code reviewer vê apenas real changes

4. **Notify user (if conflicts detected):**
   - "Branch was behind main; rebase applied with X conflicts resolved. Revalidate via tests."

## Success signal

Code review reports não mencionam "unrelated changes merged during PR dev". All diffs são focused feature changes.

## Related

- User role: solo-dev (padrão: solo, sem time)
- Worktree workflow established

frontmatter.name: qa-single-app-startup-check-before-dispatch
frontmatter.description: QA_RUN dispatch deve validar que todos 3 apps (web :3000, server :3001, chat-server :3002) estão listening. SCRUM-73 user relatou "algum app nao ta rodando"; QA esperava full stack.

memory_entries_to_create.body:
# QA Single-App Startup Check Before Dispatch

QA via bens-qa-runner espera full app stack (:3000, :3001, :3002). Se qualquer app falhar startup, QA trava ou produz confusing errors.

## Problem

SCRUM-73 Phase 8 QA_RUN: user rodou `pnpm dev`, então disparei QA. User reportou "algum app nao ta rodando". Likely: web (:3000) subiu, server/chat-server não. QA esperava :3001/:3002 disponível.

Resultado: user percepcão de "harness broken"; meu checkpoint "ready for QA?" foi answered affirmatively, mas estado real era degraded.

## How to apply

Phase 8 QA_RUN → preflight check ANTES de dispatchar bens-qa-runner:

```bash
# Valide todos os portos em paralelo
for port in 3000 3001 3002; do
  if ! nc -zv localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "succeeded"; then
    # Port down
    return SKIP_QA  # com mensagem ao user
  fi
done
# All ports up → dispatch QA_RUN
```

Alternativa (mais simples):
```bash
lsof -i :3000,:3001,:3002 | grep -c LISTEN
# Should output: 3 (ou próximo de 3)
```

**Decision tree:**

1. All 3 ports listening → Dispatch QA_RUN
2. 1-2 ports down → Retry `pnpm dev` (wait 5s) + re-check
3. Still failing → Skip QA_RUN + notify user: "Server :300X not responding. Recommend testing post-merge on main branch."

## Success signal

Phase 8 logs contêm "Ports up: 3000 ✓ 3001 ✓ 3002 ✓" ou "Server :3001 not responding; skipping QA_RUN".

User nunca experimenta QA dispatch com partial app stack.

## Related

- Phase 8: QA_RUN (bens-qa-runner dispatch)
- Memory: [[server-cors-pinned-to-3000]] (CORS issues com worktree)
- SCRUM-72 PR #321: feedback_orchestrator-qa-preflight-server-startup.md (similar)

frontmatter.name: qa-failure-recovery-offer-alternatives
frontmatter.description: Se QA_RUN falha, NÃO re-dispatch com same prompt (cria perception de loop). Ofereça alternativas ao user: fix local, skip+merge, focused retry.

memory_entries_to_create.body:
# QA Failure Recovery: Offer Alternatives

Quando QA_RUN retorna failure (visual regression, app crash, etc.), a recovery padrão deve ser CHANGE OF APPROACH, não re-execute same check.

## Problem

SCRUM-73: User mencionou "pq vc ta em looping?" quando eu re-disparei QA_RUN com same prompt após user disser "sim" ao checkpoint "ready for QA?". Technically não foi reincidência (QA rodou, retornou), mas user percepcão era de loop.

Raiz: eu não ofereci alternative paths quando QA teve issue (server startup problem).

## How to apply

Phase 8 QA_RUN → failure recovery:

```
1. Analyze failure:
   - Is it flaky (retry may pass)?
   - Is it real regression (fix required)?
   - Is it environment-related (server down, CORS, etc.)?

2. If environment-related:
   - DO NOT: dispatch same QA_RUN again
   - DO: offer options to user:
     Option A: "Fix locally now, recommend testing post-merge on main"
     Option B: "Skip QA; merge PR and run regression tests on main"
     Option C: "Identify specific scenario; dispatch focused QA with new prompt"

3. If flaky (intermittent):
   - Option A: "Retry QA now (1 attempt, then bail)"
   - Option B: "Skip QA; test on main"

4. If real regression:
   - Identify failing test
   - Option A: "Fix and re-run focused QA"
   - Option B: "Revert change and implement differently"
```

**User selects → apply chosen path.**

Never: `dispatch(same_qa_with_same_prompt)` loop.

## Success signal

User never sees "re-dispatching same QA check". QA failures always followed by decision tree + user choice.

## Related

- Phase 8: QA_RUN (bens-qa-runner)
- [[feedback_qa-single-app-startup-check-before-dispatch]] (preflight validation)

+

+

repo_changes.reason: Add Phase 8 QA_RUN preflight app startup validation + failure recovery decision tree to prevent partial-stack QA dispatch
repo_changes.diff:
@@ -XX,XX +XX,XX @@
+#### Phase 8: QA_RUN — App startup validation
+
+Before dispatching QA_RUN via bens-qa-runner:
+
+1. Run preflight check:
+   ```bash
+   # All 3 apps must be listening
+   nc -zv localhost 3000 2>&1 | grep "succeeded"
+   nc -zv localhost 3001 2>&1 | grep "succeeded"
+   nc -zv localhost 3002 2>&1 | grep "succeeded"
+   ```
+2. If any fails:
+   - Retry: `pnpm dev` (wait 5s)
+   - Re-check ports
+   - If still failing: **skip QA_RUN**, notify user: "Server :300X not responding; recommend testing post-merge on main"
+3. Only dispatch QA_RUN if all 3 ports respond
+
+**Rationale:** QA expects full app stack; partial startup causes confusing failures.
+
+#### QA_RUN failure → recovery logic
+
+If QA_RUN is dispatched and returns failure (visual regression, app crash, etc.):
+
+1. **Analyze failure:** report specific test name + assertion
+2. **Do NOT immediately re-dispatch** same QA_RUN with same prompt
+3. **Instead, offer decision to user:**
+   - Option A: "Fix locally, recommend retesting post-merge on main"
+   - Option B: "Skip QA now; merge PR and test in main branch"
+   - Option C: "Identify specific scenario; re-run QA with focused prompt"
+4. User selects → apply recovery
+
+**Rationale:** Re-dispatching same QA check with same prompt creates perception of "looping".

repo_changes.reason: Add Phase 7 CODE_REVIEW worktree rebase step to prevent branch-behind-main issues in future solo-dev PRs
repo_changes.diff:
@@ -XX,XX +XX,XX @@
+#### Phase 7: CODE_REVIEW — Worktree sync
+
+If developing in worktree (solo dev pattern):
+
+1. Before opening PR / entering CODE_REVIEW:
+   ```bash
+   git fetch origin
+   git rebase origin/main
+   ```
+2. If merge conflicts:
+   - Resolve manually
+   - Re-run tests: `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
+   - Commit resolution
+3. If rebase clean:
+   - Diff will be purely feature changes
+   - Code reviewer sees clean diffs (no "unrelated changes merged during dev")
+
+**Rationale:** Multiple PRs may merge to main during solo dev (~4.5h). Branch falls behind. Rebase before CODE_REVIEW ensures clean diff review.
